style_when: the article explains how a system, process or stack actually works — money flows, supply chains, pipelines, an agent assembly line
prompt: Clean technical isometric cutaway of a warehouse aisle inside a distribution center, axonometric projection, thin consistent line weight, flat muted style. A modular picking line runs diagonally across the frame: galvanised steel rack modules with polymer tote trays, several operator bays standing empty with their vacant positions marked in safety yellow, others fed by conveyor. Two matte autonomous mobile robots travel the same aisle, the lead robot commanding the left foreground third, brushed-steel bodies with dark polymer bumpers. The cutaway sits flat on a concrete-grey plant floor texture. One directional light rakes from the upper left, throwing long clean shadows. Palette of concrete grey, graphite and one safety-yellow accent. Unlabelled, no text, generous empty margin, asymmetric off-centre composition.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, watermarks, logos
rationale: The article is a modeling story — how operators price the labor line — so an axonometric cutaway states the mechanism the way an ops desk actually draws it. Empty picking bays make the 40% churn visible while the robot fleet shares the same aisle, literalizing retention spend competing with robot capex. It also rotates the desk's medium mix after five photographic and collage headers.
cue: A robot fleet has to beat this stream
subject: autonomous mobile robots working a warehouse picking line whose modular operator stations stand partly empty
core_thesis: A warehouse labor line is not a wage but a 40%-a-year replacement stream, so an automation payback must price labor from exit costs — and retention spend competes with robot capex for the same dollars.
core_conflict: The calm wage line hides a $21,800-per-exit churn stream; retention programs and robot fleets now bid against each other for the same operating budget, and only one sits in the capital deck.
composition: Asymmetric off-centre layout: picking line runs diagonally across the lower two-thirds, lead robot commanding the left foreground, empty bays receding to the right, generous empty margin above
